source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-13

procedures.title: Delcotron diode and field test
steps: The meter should show high resistance one way and low the other.
Negative diodes (test B): read between the "R" and "GRD" terminals, reverse leads and read again; again expect high one way, low the other.
A high reading both ways or a low reading both ways means a bad diode.
Open field check: on the lowest range, read from the "F" terminal to the "GRD" stud; it should be 7 to 20 ohms.
Zero or very high resistance means the Delcotron is faulty.
If any test shows a bad Delcotron, remove it and check it fully per Service Operations.

procedures.title: Indicator lamp / initial field excitation circuit: test
steps: Normal: the lamp lights with ignition ON and goes out almost as soon as the engine starts. Ammeter cars use the same circuit without the lamp.

If the lamp does not light or the ammeter does nothing, suspect: bad bulb or socket, bad ammeter, open circuit in wiring, regulator or field, or a shorted positive diode (which can also light the lamp with ignition OFF).
Step 1: unplug the regulator connector, turn ignition ON and connect a test lamp from connector terminal "4" to ground (see figure 11c in the manual).
If the test lamp stays dark, look for a bad bulb, socket or open wire between switch and regulator connector and repair.
If it lights, the fault is in the regulator, the Delcotron, or the wire between the "F" terminals of regulator and Delcotron; go to step 2.
